answer: Admit a newcomer only if it sits within a short graph distance of several established anchors that are themselves far apart. A sybil cluster is dense inside but distant from most anchors, like nectar pooled in one flower while a willow's roots reach many separate streams; fakes cannot fake closeness to far-flung anchors without building real relationships, so attack cost grows with each anchor. Limits: newcomers in sparse regions struggle, and a patient attacker can slowly grow copper-strong chains toward each anchor, so distances must be recomputed often.
